items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: I was listening to WGMC and Sonny Rollins was playing “Blue Room.”

ctx.x: sometimes played a lot of notes, but when you really painstakingly learn one of the Parker solos, you can hear that every one of those notes make sense, and that one phrase really has something to do with the phrase before or with the phrase that’s coming afterwards. And very often the key notes in those phrases, the top note or the longest note, may even be the note that happens to be there in the original melody. But you have to get to more than just a completely superficial understanding of music before you…
That’s interesting because on the way down here I was listening to WGMC and Sonny Rollins was playing “Blue Room.”
